review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it depends on: CanonicalDrift.outerLimit and its lemmas. I also grepped the SpanningForest directory for how sibling `drift` definitions are unfolded. The file declares no @[simp] lemmas and has no simp-set conflicts or loops. The only simp-interface issue I found is that `drift` has no unfolding lemma, so call sites unfold it by hand with `change`. I did not check downstream uses outside the SpanningForest directory, because Main.lean and DecoderBundle.lean only import the file. I could not run Lean, so the replacement is untested.

findings.excerpt:
change Measurable (fun p : ℝ × (ι → ℝ) =>
      Filter.limsup (fun n => f n a p.1 p.2 j) atTop)
findings.problem: `drift` is a plain `def` over `CanonicalDrift.outerLimit`, which is itself a plain `def` over `Filter.limsup`. The file gives no unfolding or evaluation lemma, so users must reduce it by hand. `decode_integral_equation` does this with a `change` that restates the `limsup` form, and it also uses `unfold drift` in other lemmas. Sibling drift definitions (PosteriorDrift, IntrinsicTreeDrift, GraphTreePosteriorEquiv) do the same with `simp only [drift, ..., CanonicalDrift.outerLimit, ...]`. Every consumer must therefore know the two-layer definitional structure and restate the `limsup` form. That is brittle and makes `simp` unable to normalise `drift f a t y i`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a reducible-by-`simp` equation lemma next to the definition, for example `lemma drift_def (f) (a) (t) (y) (i) : drift f a t y i = Filter.limsup (fun n => f n a t y i) atTop := rfl`. Tag it `@[simp]` only if you want the `limsup` form to be the normal form. Otherwise keep it as a named lemma used via `simp only [drift_def]` or `rw`. Then `hm` in `decode_integral_equation` can be `fun j => Measurable.limsup fun n => (hf n j).comp hp`, or can use `measurable_drift` composed with `hp`. The `change` and the `unfold drift` calls go away. Downstream files can drop the `CanonicalDrift.outerLimit` unfolding too.
findings.benefit: The `limsup` unfolding lives in one lemma instead of being restated as `change`/`unfold` goals in several files. Proofs no longer depend on how `drift` and `outerLimit` are layered, and `simp only [drift_def]` becomes a stable entry point.
